comparisons.peer_topic: Definition and Scope of Operational Risk
comparisons.peer_summary: Operational risk is defined as the risk of adverse outcomes from inadequate internal processes, systems, human factors, or external events, and explicitly includes compliance, conduct, legal, and estimations and model risk.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPM explicitly define the scope of operational risk to include specific sub-risks. GS identifies operational risk as one of the inherent risk categories in its businesses and references detailed management sections, including 'Operational Risk Management' and 'Model Risk Management'. JPM defines operational risk as outcomes from inadequate processes/systems/human factors/external events and explicitly lists 'compliance, conduct, legal, and estimations and model risk' as included subcategories. Both firms treat model and compliance/conduct risks as integral components of their operational risk framework.

sentences.text: Risks are inherent in our businesses and include liquidity, market, credit, operational, cybersecurity, model, legal, compliance, conduct, regulatory and reputational risks.

For further information about our risk management processes, see "Overview and Structure of Risk Management," and for information about our areas of risk, see "Liquidity Risk Management," "Market Risk Management," "Credit Risk Management," "Operational Risk Management," "Cybersecurity Risk Management," "Model Risk Management" and "Other Risk Management," as well as "Risk Factors" in Part I, Item 1A of this Form 10-K.
Operational risk is the risk of an adverse outcome resulting from inadequate or failed internal processes or systems; human factors; or external events impacting the Firm's processes or systems.
Operational Risk includes compliance, conduct, legal, and estimations and model risk.

comparisons.peer_topic: Scope of Risk Management and Principal Risk Types
comparisons.peer_summary: Policies cover Institutional Securities, Wealth Management, Investment Management, significant operating subsidiaries, and the Parent Company level. Principal risks identified are both financial and non-financial, including market (including non-trading interest rate risk), credit, liquidity, model, operational (including cybersecurity), compliance (including conduct), financial crimes, strategic, and reputational risks. Strategic risk is integrated into business planning and overseen by the Board.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and MS provide a comprehensive list of the principal risks inherent in their business operations. GS states that risks are inherent and include 'liquidity, market, credit, operational, cybersecurity, model, legal, compliance, conduct, regulatory and reputational risks.' MS similarly identifies principal risks as both financial and non-financial, including 'market... credit, liquidity, model, operational (including cybersecurity), compliance (including conduct)... and reputational risks.' Both disclosures highlight the inclusion of cybersecurity within operational risk and conduct/compliance within compliance risk, demonstrating a similar taxonomy of inherent business risks.

sentences.text: Risks are inherent in our businesses and include liquidity, market, credit, operational, cybersecurity, model, legal, compliance, conduct, regulatory and reputational risks.

The principal risks involved in our business activities are both financial and non-financial and include market (including non-trading interest rate risk), credit, liquidity, model, operational (including cybersecurity), compliance (including conduct), financial crimes, strategic and reputational risks.
